svg.title: From 10,000 Screened Parcels to 17 Completed Exits
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-annual-parcel-cohort-conversion; chart type: funnel; title: From 10,000 Screened Parcels to 17 Completed Exits; subtitle: One nested annual cohort supporting the mature Base-Case model; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage and counts unique parcel opportunities, not emails, owner contacts, or repeat offers. This illustrative mature-year cohort assumes its 17 acquisitions also resell within the modeled year at $50,000 each. Actual acquisition and disposition cohorts can cross reporting years.; caption: 17 completed parcel sales × $50,000 = $850,000 gross annual revenue. This is a steady-state illustration, not a first-month closing target; time to first deal remains 3–9 months.; stages: label: Parcels screened; value: 10,000 unique opportunities; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Deduplicate assessor parcel identifiers and remove public land, incompatible parcel sizes, and obvious geographic mismatches. This starting population supplies the denominator for the complete conversion funnel.; label: Desktop-qualified parcels; value: 2,000 parcels; 20% advance; numeric value: 2000.0; detail: Retain parcels with plausible access, usable terrain, supporting sale comparables, and an identifiable owner. Desktop qualification does not replace title review or establish environmental suitability.; label: Seller-engaged parcels; value: 400 parcels; 20% advance; numeric value: 400.0; detail: Count an opportunity only after the owner or authorized representative responds substantively about that parcel. Record price expectations, ownership authority, timing, and disclosed property issues before preparing terms.; label: Written offers issued; value: 100 parcels; 25% advance; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Issue written offers only where preliminary economics survive transaction expenses and holding costs. Maintain one cohort entry per parcel even when price or inspection terms are revised.; label: Acquired and resold; value: 17 parcels; 17% advance; numeric value: 17.0; detail: Complete diligence, insured acquisition, and subsequent sale for 17 parcels: 0.17% of the original cohort. Count gross completed-sale proceeds rather than pending contracts, listing prices, or unrealized appreciation.

text.title: From 10,000 Screened Parcels to 17 Completed Exits
text.tspan: From 10,000 Screened Parcels to 17 Completed Exits

circle.title: label: Parcels screened; value: 10,000 unique opportunities; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Deduplicate assessor parcel identifiers and remove public land, incompatible parcel sizes, and obvious geographic mismatches. This starting population supplies the denominator for the complete conversion funnel.

label: Desktop-qualified parcels; value: 2,000 parcels; 20% advance; numeric value: 2000.0; detail: Retain parcels with plausible access, usable terrain, supporting sale comparables, and an identifiable owner. Desktop qualification does not replace title review or establish environmental suitability.

label: Seller-engaged parcels; value: 400 parcels; 20% advance; numeric value: 400.0; detail: Count an opportunity only after the owner or authorized representative responds substantively about that parcel. Record price expectations, ownership authority, timing, and disclosed property issues before preparing terms.

label: Written offers issued; value: 100 parcels; 25% advance; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Issue written offers only where preliminary economics survive transaction expenses and holding costs. Maintain one cohort entry per parcel even when price or inspection terms are revised.

label: Acquired and resold; value: 17 parcels; 17% advance; numeric value: 17.0; detail: Complete diligence, insured acquisition, and subsequent sale for 17 parcels: 0.17% of the original cohort. Count gross completed-sale proceeds rather than pending contracts, listing prices, or unrealized appreciation.

text.title: Assumptions: Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage and counts unique parcel opportunities, not emails, owner contacts, or repeat offers. This illustrative mature-year cohort assumes its 17 acquisitions also resell within the modeled year at $50,000 each. Actual acquisition and disposition cohorts can cross reporting years.
